entry.title: On This Day — August 17
entry.content: • 986 – Byzantine–Bulgarian wars: Battle of the Gates of Trajan: The Bulgarians under the Comitopuli Samuel and Aron defeat the Byzantine forces at the Gate of Trajan, with Byzantine Emperor Basil II barely escaping. • 1186 – Georgenberg Pact: Ottokar IV, Duke of Styria and Leopold V, Duke of Austria sign a heritage agreement in which Ottokar gives his duchy to Leopold and to his son Frederick under the stipulation that Austria and Styria would henceforth remain undivided. • 1386 – Karl Topia, the ruler of Princedom of Albania, forges an alliance with the Republic of Venice, committing to participate in all wars of the Republic and receiving coastal protection against the Ottomans in return. • 1424 – Hundred Years' War: Battle of Verneuil: An English force under John, Duke of Bedford defeats a larger French army under Jean II, Duke of Alençon, John Stewart, and Earl Archibald of Douglas. • 1488 – Konrad Bitz, the Bishop of Turku, marks the date of his preface to Missale Aboense, the oldest known book of Finland.

entry.title: Product of the Day — An Ozkan Book Of Wisdoms
entry.content:
The An Ozkan Book Of Wisdoms is a collection of cryptic notes scribbled by a mysterious individual known only as 'Ozkan'. Pages appear at random intervals, filled with enigmatic advice and prophecies. As readers pour over the texts, phrases seem to shift and rearrange themselves according to their personal fears and desires. Those who decipher the secrets within claim it grants unparalleled insight into future events – though skeptics dismiss it as mere coincidences.
It's said those who spend extended periods studying The Book develop an uncanny ability to predict mundane occurrences weeks ahead of time, such as when their neighbors will mow their lawns again or which days the local bakery has fresh croissants available.
Categories: books
